text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on vast amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence based on patterns they learned from this data, allowing them to generate human-like text. To get good results, users practice prompt engineering—asking clear, specific questions or giving detailed instructions. LLMs can summarize information, write stories, or help with coding, which makes them useful tools. However, they have limits: they can make mistakes, lack true understanding, and sometimes produce confident but incorrect answers. They also cannot access real-time information unless connected to the internet. So, while powerful, they should be used critically, with human checking of important facts.
